cells.tense: The ground has just cleared, and you are standing in it with your hands full.
cells.ask: Name one thing the clearing made possible, then hand one piece of it to someone and let them carry it with you.
cells.core:
The ground is clear and you're standing in it, keeping what broke open from sliding away. Nobody told you the room would look like this afterward, and you're not pretending otherwise. You kept it because it mattered, not because anyone required it, so the shape it has now is the shape you gave it.

That's a plain kind of keeping — deciding what survives the clearing and living with the choice. Nothing is owed to anyone about it yet. Hand a piece to somebody and it comes back a little different; watching that happen tells you what you actually want to keep. The thing is yours either way, and so is the timing of when it goes out.
cells.sheetLine: The ground is clear and you're standing in it, keeping what matters.
cells.verb: holding steady on what the break just cleared
cells.place: at the open ground where a false structure has just come down

cells.tense: You're building the walls up higher than the house next door has ever needed.
cells.ask: Set down one thing you're guarding that nobody has threatened, leave it overnight, and notice the morning without it.
cells.core:
You're keeping everything a little too hard. Not the pieces that matter — the ones that might, someday, if the ground gives way. All this guarding is aimed at trouble that hasn't shown up, and it's making the room tighter than it needs to be.

When this goes well it looks like nothing. Something real comes through a change you didn't ask for, and you hold it without gripping — present, unhurried, still able to reach the people in front of you. What's happening now leans past them into a day that hasn't arrived. Let one thing settle on its own overnight, and check on it in daylight. It's still there in the morning, and you'll have spent the night as a person instead of a watch.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping hard against trouble that hasn't arrived.

cells.tense: The clearing came through a while back, and you are standing at a door it already closed.
cells.ask: Write down one thing the last six months changed, then move one object or one appointment so it matches.
cells.core:
You don't pick it up. Something came through the change and you haven't stood behind it — the footing isn't there, and the day you're describing isn't the day you're in. You know the shape of the old thing better than the shape of the new one.

Going well, this is ordinary. Something settles, you plant yourself beside it, and it holds because you're there — the feeling arrives as you go, not before you start. The reach doesn't come. Put one visible fact down that says the change already happened. Matching something small to what you know keeps more than thinking about it.
cells.sheetLine: The change already came through, and you're at the old door.

cells.tense: You are the one keeping this steady, and you are calling it luck or timing.
cells.ask: Tell one person one piece of what you've kept that you chose or built, and say plainly that you're the reason it's here.
cells.core:
You've been holding the line as if nobody in particular were doing it. When the old shape came down, the thing worth saving stayed up, and the calm in the room is your calm — but the story you tell is that the day brought it. Your part in it went unnamed.

Working right, this is simply structure that serves what it holds. Things stand, people can lean on them, and it doesn't need announcing. There's a groundedness in that, and a quiet room. What's missing is the one sentence. Tell a person what you made before the credit drifts to chance.
cells.sheetLine: You kept it, and you're calling it luck.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a clearing already happened and left something worth guarding; the record only says the capacity to preserve what transformation produced is seated in breakthrough, not that a particular ending has occurred. A reader could reasonably say nothing has broken open for them — that the seat is quiet, not arrived at. The asks survive being wrong: each is a small, visible act that is still useful if the reading mistakes the person's situation, and none ties progress to accepting the frame. The sentence that serves the writer is the one that treats the settled thing as already there; it reads as insight and is the one I have to be most careful with.
